page: The Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-3200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance provisioned on an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by vector instruction support including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. Hardware acceleration for cryptographic routines is provided via AES and SHA-NI flags. The server operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Memory allocation stands at 256.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio that aligns with memory-optimized architectures. In uncached large-block benchmarks, memory bandwidth reaches 444.47 GB/sec for read-only operations and 197.86 GB/sec for writes, both falling within the top 10 percent of tested systems. Local storage is provided as a bundled 3200 GB NVMe SSD volume, eliminating the immediate need for external block storage pools.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate robust parallel compute and data manipulation metrics. The system attained a PassMark CPU score of 63,813.51 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 100,562.57, placing in the top 25 percent. In-memory data throughput is highlighted by 71.28 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 208.52 GB/sec. Conversely, general web serving throughput (28.25 GB/sec) and single-core Geekbench evaluation (1,867.0) align with middle-tier performance tiers.

This server type presents a balanced tradeoff favoring high memory capacity, dense NVMe storage, and memory subsystem bandwidth over bleeding-edge single-threaded clock frequencies. It is well-suited for memory-resident caching clusters, database engines, continuous integration compilation tasks, and medium-scale localized data processing workflows.
description: The Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-3200s-amd is a memory-oriented server in the Optimized Cloud Compute lineup, configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs on a 16-core AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. With 256.0 GB of RAM, the instance delivers an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and top-tier large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 444.47 GB/sec. The instance includes 3200 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and excludes discrete GPUs. Benchmark results emphasize strong multi-core processing with a PassMark CPU score of 63,813.51, top-quartile Redis SET performance at 71.28 million operations per second, and strong software compilation throughput. This hardware profile suits in-memory databases, large caching layers, distributed compilation, and data-intensive analytics that require substantial memory bandwidth alongside direct-attached high-speed NVMe storage.
